haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes to the separate shadow store, never charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store, so it stays current, but never charges.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch and 5000+ invoices compared. A person must advance it one step at a time; meeting the gate never triggers the move.
haiku-low.q4: Charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window starts rollback automatically, in both or new_only modes. Shadow has no automatic trigger; on-call starts it by hand.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback always ends in old_only, and is never retried into another mode. Afterward a person must advance to shadow again, and the 7-day count restarts at zero.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback from new_only is possible through day 34 and refused from day 35. The usage event log keeps events only 35 days, and the old engine may be decommissioned.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED. The document only says billing_mode lives in the config service; how workers learn of changes and what happens to an in-flight invoice is not stated.
haiku-low.q8: In the rollout bookkeeping record beside the billing_mode flag. Forward moves need a person, one step at a time, with no skipping, and meeting a gate never triggers the move.
haiku-low.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. It measures charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window, and when met it starts rollback automatically and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Charges that fall due stay pending during ReconcileCharges, for the old engine to pick up. The old engine actually makes them at the ResumeOldEngine step, after reconciliation and any reprocessing.
haiku-low.q11: A unique ledger key of customer and billing period. Both engines check and write it before charging, so duplicates fail, and the old engine skips periods already recorded. Freezing new charging first prevents overlap.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in RollingBack, with the recorded step and reason saved. The controller resumes from that step on restart; each step is safe to repeat, and the ledger key blocks a second charge.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes to the shadow store only (never charges, never writes the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine still computes every invoice, into the shadow store, and never charges.
sonnet.q3: 7 consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch and 5000+ invoices compared. A person advances; nothing is automatic and meeting the gate does not trigger the move.
sonnet.q4: A charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window. It can happen in both and new_only (before day 35). Shadow has no auto trigger; shadow errors never roll back.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over, a person must advance to shadow again, and the 7-day count restarts at zero (gates are reset).
sonnet.q6: From day 35 in new_only. The old engine may be decommissioned and there is no way back. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so the skipped events needed for reprocessing may be gone. Manual rollback is refused and an auto-trigger means alert on-call and fix forward.
sonnet.q8: NOT STATED as a single place for all evidence. The document says only that rollout bookkeeping is a durable record next to the flag (holding the consecutive-day count, unresolved-mismatch count and Finance sign-off), and that gates are preconditions that a person checks. It does not say any mechanism blocks an early promotion.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED. The document gives the trigger (charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window) and the response (start rollback automatically and page on-call), but does not name the detecting component.
sonnet.q10: A charge due but not made stays pending for the old engine to pick up. It is made once the old engine resumes at ResumeOldEngine.
sonnet.q11: The ledger's unique key per customer and billing period. Both engines check and write it before charging, so a duplicate attempt fails. The old engine also skips customer-periods already in the ledger. Ambiguous in-flight attempts are looked up at the provider first.
sonnet.q12: The state is recorded, so the rollback stays in RollingBack at the recorded step. After a crash the controller resumes from the recorded step. Each step must be safe to repeat, and the ledger key prevents a second charge. The document does not describe any other state beyond that.
